title: Record the comment-only wiring mutant, which proves the extraction's comment-stripping load-bearing
description: opum-doc ODOC-218 ran a mutant OMARK-60 did not: the env mapping present ONLY AS A COMMENT, with the guard disabled underneath. This is lore-web instruction-versus-explanation trap applied to the new assertion - the job comments explain the design and so contain the very strings the check greps for, meaning a whole-file grep would be satisfied by PROSE while the guard is fully disabled. Worst possible combination for a check whose job is to notice exactly that. Measured here rather than reasoned: commented both mappings out and repointed BEFORE_SHA to github.sha underneath -> DIED, 2 red. So the sed s/#.*// and the awk job-scoping in the extraction are load-bearing. They were inherited from the earlier run:/fetch-depth wiring checks and were never measured in that role.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The mutation record carries the comment-only mapping mutant and its result, naming what it proves about the extraction rather than about the workflow
The wiring section says why the extraction is comment-stripped and job-scoped, so a later author does not simplify it to a whole-file grep

finalSummary: Delivered in PR #127. Mutant from opum-doc ODOC-218, run here rather than taken from their report: env mappings left ONLY as comments with BEFORE_SHA repointed to github.sha underneath -> DIED, 2 red. It is the only mutant in the record whose death is caused by the extraction (sed 's/#.*//' plus awk job-scoping) rather than by an assertion, so it measures the extraction and is recorded as such. Those two were inherited from the earlier run:/fetch-depth checks and had never been measured in that role. Comment added at the site telling a later author not to simplify either away, with lore-web's instruction-versus-explanation reason: the job's own comments explain this wiring and so contain the exact strings grepped for.
